correctness.rationale: The normalized erased state factor is idempotent with exact token annihilation. In an orthonormal plane adapted to the key and scaled key its nontrivial block is [[0,-tau/mu],[0,1]], so its Euclidean norm is ||Dk||/mu for every dimension at least two. The endpoint polynomial inequality d_i^2 <= (kappa+1)d_i-kappa gives a sharp upper bound C_kappa=(kappa+1)/(2 sqrt(kappa)) on each factor, hence on every N-product by submultiplicativity. Unit keys (1,t)/sqrt(1+t^2) and (t,1)/sqrt(1+t^2) with switched endpoint diagonals give P1=C a b^T, P2=P1^T=C b a^T, and exact alternating products C^N a a^T or C^N a b^T; their norms match the bound for every N. Orthogonal direct-sum padding proves the statement for all d>=2 and kappa=1 is handled. The original standalone verifier was actually executed, including 630 exact-rational identities and 48000 finite random comparisons; the computations supplement, not replace, the proof.

originality.rationale: The main motivating full text defines diagonal write-side key scaling and establishes a token-local residual-ratio theorem, not worst-case growth of products of homogeneous state transitions. Classical oblique-projector norm identities and Kantorovich inequalities give individual-factor control, but not the attained finite-horizon rate for every N in this particular bounded diagonal switching family. Inspected full-text weighted projection literature imposes block-iteration weighting constraints and does not imply the arbitrary-product statement. No equivalent published-finding corpus claim or published source was located by the specified actual searches; this is qualified by the residual risks.
residual_risks: An older angle-inequality or product-of-oblique-projections paper could already contain an equivalent sharp arbitrary-length formula; searching is not a proof of uniqueness.

The full text of Censor–Elfving (2002) was not accessible, so its complete possible implications could not be inspected. Its accessible abstract and the full 2003 related paper do not resolve that risk decisively.

The conclusion assumes unconstrained arbitrary admissible switching, whereas any particular online hypergradient rule generates a smaller correlated family; the result cannot by itself predict practical instability.

value.rationale: The theorem completely determines the sharp worst-case finite-horizon stability envelope for a motivated online preconditioned memory update under an interpretable diagonal condition ratio. It exposes a structural gap between perfect token-local least-squares correction and sequence-level control: even with unit keys, two positive diagonal weights bounded by 2, and admissible gate 3/4, an exact two-token word multiplies a persistent state by 9/8. This is a natural complete classification and explicit boundary, not a numerical benchmark or an arbitrary parameter slice. The theorem identifies a reason to consider shared-metric or sequence-level safeguards while avoiding unsupported claims about the source paper’s actual learned controller.
